text:
Thoughts
expand_more
1. Specific B001 Comparison Passages
Because this source is a primary critical edition of the Greek text with a variant-recording apparatus rather than an exegetical commentary, none of the twelve B001 passages contain editorial discussion of Old Testament intertextuality, Hebrew/Greek translational ambiguities, or oral/liturgical transmission.
Where a textual variation unit exists in the apparatus for that specific verse, the competing textual forms and editorial disagreements are extracted below; otherwise, NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE is recorded
1
more_horiz
.
1. Romans 4:3 / Genesis 15:6
Page / Locator: Page 317
1
Citation:
1
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. The apparatus records variants for Romans 4:1 and 4:2, but contains no textual note, competing reading, or discussion for verse 3
1
.
2. Romans 9:25 / Hosea 2:23
Page / Locator: Page 326
2
Citation:
2
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. No textual note or discussion occurs at verse 25
2
.
3. Romans 9:26 / Hosea 1:10
Page / Locator: Page 326
2
Citation:
2
Competing Textual Form / Disagreement:
Textual Note: 26 αὐτοῖς WH NIV RP ] – Treg
2
.
Details: Samuel Tregelles omits the pronoun αὐτοῖς, whereas Westcott–Hort, NIV, Robinson–Pierpont, and Holmes include it
2
.
Other Categories (Uncertainty, Hebrew/Greek ambiguity, oral/liturgical transmission, weakening evidence): NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE.
4. Romans 10:11 / Isaiah 28:16
Page / Locator: Page 327
3
Citation:
3
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. No textual note or discussion occurs at verse 11
3
.
5. Romans 10:13 / Joel 2:32
Page / Locator: Page 327
3
Citation:
3
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. No textual note or discussion occurs at verse 13
3
.
6. Romans 11:34 / Isaiah 40:13
Page / Locator: Page 329
4
Citation:
4
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. No textual note or discussion occurs at verse 34
4
.
7. Romans 15:12 / Isaiah 11:10
Page / Locator: Page 334
5
Citation:
5
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. No textual note or discussion occurs at verse 12
5
.
8. 1 Corinthians 1:19 / Isaiah 29:14
Page / Locator: Page 339
6
Citation:
6
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. The apparatus records variants for 1:20, 1:22, and 1:23, but none for verse 19
6
.
9. 1 Corinthians 6:16 / Genesis 2:24
Page / Locator: Page 344
7
Citation:
7
Competing Textual Form / Disagreement:
Textual Note: 16 ἦ WH Treg NIV ] – RP
7
.
Details: The Byzantine textform (Robinson–Pierpont) omits the introductory disjunctive particle ἦ, while Westcott–Hort, Tregelles, NIV, and Holmes include it
7
.
Other Categories: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE.
10. 1 Corinthians 9:9 / Deuteronomy 25:4
Page / Locator: Page 349
8
Citation:
8
Competing Textual Form / Disagreement:
Textual Note: 9 κημώσεις Treg NIV ] φιμώσεις WH RP
8
.
Details: Holmes adopts κημώσεις with Tregelles and NIV, disagreeing with Westcott–Hort and the Byzantine text (RP), which read φιμώσεις
8
.
Other Categories: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE.
11. 1 Corinthians 10:7 / Exodus 32:6
Page / Locator: Page 350
9
Citation:
9
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. No textual note or discussion occurs at verse 7
9
.
12. Galatians 3:13 / Deuteronomy 21:23
Page / Locator: Page 382
10
Citation:
10
Competing Textual Form / Disagreement:
Textual Note: 13 ὅτι γέγραπται WH Treg NIV ] γέγραπται γάρ RP
10
.
Details: In the citation formula introducing the curse from Deuteronomy, Robinson–Pierpont reads γέγραπται γάρ, whereas Westcott–Hort, Tregelles, NIV, and Holmes print ὅτι γέγραπται
10
.
Other Categories: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE.
2. General Editorial, Methodological, and Text-Critical Disclosures
Across the front matter (Preface, Introduction) and Appendix, the editor explicitly addresses several of the queried categories in establishing the New Testament text:
A. Expresses Uncertainty / Editorial Doubt
Doubtful Text Indicated by Brackets:
Page / Locator: Page xiv, Symbols Used in the Text
11
.
Citation:
11
Statement: Single square brackets [ ] indicate that "The enclosed text is doubtful"
11
.
Uncertainty Over Verse Status (Acts 19:41):
Page / Locator: Page xiv, Footnote 14
11
.
Citation:
11
Statement: A 41st verse number was placed in brackets (
12
) at the end of Acts 19 "to indicate uncertainty regarding its status"
11
.
Severe Limitation on Bracketing to Avoid Evading Hard Choices:
Page / Locator: Page xv, Footnote 16
13
.
Citation:
13
Statement: Holmes notes that brackets were used only six times in the entire New Testament (Luke 22:19–20; 24:40; 24:51; 24:52; Eph 1:1; Col 1:20)
13
. He explains that brackets have been overused "as what could be perceived as a means of avoiding difficult choices", whereas an editor's duty is "to make choices, particularly in the 'hard cases'"
13
.
Subjectivity of Proper Noun Capitalization:
Page / Locator: Page xiii, Footnote 13
14
.
Citation:
14
Statement: Deciding proper noun capitalization is explicitly described as "A category that offers, to be sure, numerous opportunities for differences of opinion"
14
.
ECM Uncertainty Markers (Appendix):
Page / Locator: Page 515, Appendix Footnote 1
15
.
Citation:
15
Statement: Holmes explains that bold dots in the Editio Critica Maior designate "alternative readings which were considered of equal value" or instances where reasons for a primary reading were superior "but not sufficiently to rule out with complete confidence the claims of the indicated alternative reading"
15
.
B. Discusses Competing Textual Forms
Scope of Documented Variation Units:
Page / Locator: Page xi and Page xv
13
more_horiz
.
Citation:
13
more_horiz
Statement: The edition records all differences across 6,928 variation units between the SBL text and WH, Treg, NIV, RP, and NA (excluding purely orthographical matters)
13
more_horiz
.
Westcott and Hort Double Brackets for Ancient Non-Original Material:
Page / Locator: Page xvi and Page xxi
18
19
.
Citation:
18
19
Statement: The apparatus preserves WH's double brackets (〚WH〛), marking passages (such as Luke 22:43–44) that WH "did not think belonged to the genuine text but that they did not feel free to remove completely from their printed text due to its antiquity or intrinsic interest"
18
19
.
C. Notes a Hebrew/Greek Ambiguity
Findings: NONE FOUND IN THIS SOURCE. The editor nowhere analyzes Hebrew versus Greek linguistic, translational, or Septuagintal ambiguities in the introductory matter or textual notes.
D. Allows Authorial Adaptation, Oral Transmission, Liturgical Transmission, or Unknown Textual Forms
Historical Alteration by Communities:
Page / Locator: Page viii, Preface
20
.
Citation:
20
Statement: The editor states that studying variant readings illuminates "how particular individuals and faith communities adopted, used, and sometimes altered the texts that they read, studied, and transmitted"
20
.
Definition of Target Text as Initial Circulating Form:
Page / Locator: Page xi, Footnote 8
16
.
Citation:
16
Statement: Holmes defines the goal of his edition as determining "which variant most likely represents the form in which the text first began to be copied and to circulate"
16
.
Liturgical Doxological Additions in Apparatus:
Page / Locator: Page 10 (Matthew 6:13 apparatus)
21
; Page 337 (Romans 16:24 apparatus)
22
.
Citation:
21
22
Statement: The apparatus records traditional liturgical/doxological additions preserved in the Byzantine textform (RP), such as the conclusion to the Lord's Prayer (+ Ὅτι σοῦ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία... RP in Matt 6:13) and the closing benediction in Rom 16:24 (Ἡ χάρις … ὑμῶν RP ] – WH Treg NIV)
21
22
.
E. Disagrees with Another Scholar or Edition
Disagreement with the Standard Modern Text (NA/UBS):
Page / Locator: Page viii, Preface
20
.
Citation:
20
Statement: The SBLGNT "differs from the standard text in more than 540 variation units"
20
.
Departures from All Four Primary Reference Editions:
Page / Locator: Page xi, Footnote 9
23
.
Citation:
23
Statement: Holmes preferred a reading not found in any of the four primary editions (WH, Treg, NIV, RP) in 56 variation units
23
. In 38 of these, the reading was supported by marginal notes in WH, Treg, or NA
23
.
Rejection of Universal Agreement in 1 Corinthians 12:10:
Page / Locator: Page xxi
24
.
Citation:
24
Statement: In 1 Corinthians 12:10, Holmes prints the asyndetic reading ἄλλῳ against all four primary editions (+ δὲ WH Treg NIV RP)
24
.
Disagreement with BDAG Orthography (Colossians 2:16):
Page / Locator: Page xiii, Footnote 11
25
.
Citation:
25
Statement: Holmes departs from BDAG's spelling by printing νουμηνίας rather than νεομηνίας in Colossians 2:16
25
.
Disagreement with the UBS Editorial Committee Majority (Phil 3:21):
Page / Locator: Page xii, Footnote 10
26
.
Citation:
26
Statement: In agreement with a minority of the UBS committee against the majority, the SBLGNT prints rough breathings on forms of αὐτός where exegetically reflexive
26
.
Disagreements with the Editio Critica Maior (Catholic Letters):
Page / Locator: Pages 515–516, Appendix
27
28
.
Citation:
27
28
Statement: In the Catholic Letters, Holmes enumerates 39 specific places where the SBLGNT differs from the text of the ECM
27
28
.
F. Acknowledges Evidence That Weakens the Preferred Interpretation
Bias of Bracketing Toward Inclusion:
Page / Locator: Page xv, Footnote 16
13
.
Citation:
13
Statement: Holmes acknowledges that decisions on doubtful text are made "for better or worse", citing David C. Parker's concept of "wise reticence" and admitting that the availability of brackets inherently "biases the decision-making process toward inclusion (one can bracket an included word about which one has some degree of doubt... but one cannot bracket the omission of a word about which one has an equal degree of doubt)"
13
.
Rejection of Textual Finality:
Page / Locator: Page vii–viii, Preface
20
29
.
Citation:
20
29
Statement: Holmes explicitly cautions against viewing any printed critical text as a "final" text, affirming that it must be treated as a "working" text open to continual verification, revision, and improvement
20
29
.
🔍 Would you like to inspect any of the 56 specific variation units where Holmes adopted a reading differing from all four primary reference editions?
